newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Embraer issues $70 mln in debt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Embraer issues $70 mln in debt.

text.p: Brazilian airplane maker Embraer said it has issued $70 million in commercial paper backed by anticipated revenues from the future delivery of two EMB-145 aircraft to U.S.-based Continental Express.

"This kind of issue of commercial notes is an alternative that allows us to raise funds at competitive costs and gives Embraer access to international financial markets," Embraer President Mauricio Botelho was quoted as saying in a statement.
The commercial paper was issued May 19 and pays quarterly based on a 10.25 percent annual yield. The paper matures Aug 3, 1998, the statement said.
The Embraer statement did not specify where the commerical paper was placed, and a company spokesman was not immediately available to provide that information.
The issue was the first tranche of a planned $200 million program. It was co-lead-managed by Brazil-based Bozano, Simonsen Securities and Banco do Brasil's BB Securities, the Embraer statement said.
The dates of future tranches have not been set, it said.
Continental Express, a subsidiary of Continental Airlines, signed a contract in September 1996 to buy 25 EMB-145 planes for $375 million with an option to buy an additional 175 aircraft, it said.
If all 200 planes are bought, Embraer would rake in some $2.6 billion in sales revenues.
